pages.title: What it does
text: It drives the vanilla minecraft:movement_speed attribute. A player's base is 0.1, which is about 4.317 m/s of walking speed.
This mod no longer limits movement speed: the ceiling follows the attribute's own range (vanilla 1024, higher with an attribute-range mod such as AttributeFix).

The vanilla server does have a "moved too quickly" check: on 1.21.1 it uses a fixed threshold that does not read the attribute, roughly 46x vanilla speed, and triggering it only teleports you back and logs a warning - it does not kick you. That is a vanilla mechanic, not this mod's cap.
The movement_speed.hard_cap_attr option defaults to 0 (disabled); an admin who wants a local backstop can set it to any positive value.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +0.006666667 per point.
The old curve, gain = 0.4 * x / (x + 60), had an initial slope of 0.4/60 = 0.006666667, so the early feel is unchanged.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: +2.5% per point, on the TOTAL basis.
TOTAL means the percentage scales base 0.1 + equipment (vanilla has no speed gear) + the result of the flat line.
Worked example: 20 flat + 20 percent -> (0.1 + 0.1333) * (1 + 50%) = 0.35, about 3.5x vanilla.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: There is no designed ceiling and no diminishing returns: the attribute value climbs until it meets the attribute's own range (vanilla 1024).
What you meet first is actually the vanilla server's "moved too quickly" pull-back (a fixed threshold, about 46x vanilla speed). It only teleports you back and logs a warning; it does not kick you.
Set your own comfort limit: 5x to 8x vanilla (attribute 0.5..0.8) is plenty; beyond that it starts hurting combat footwork and building precision.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: 5x to 8x vanilla (attribute 0.5..0.8) is plenty; beyond that it starts hurting combat footwork and building precision.
It is an efficiency stat: great for travelling, exploring and dodging, but it adds no combat power.
Remember that it also magnifies your momentum after a jump, so leave extra room when landing.
